source.title: On the Scaling Laws of Geographical Representation in Language Models
source.authors: Nathan Godey; Éric de la Clergerie; Benoît Sagot

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how a different outcome—geographical probing performance—changes with model scale, rather than measuring pretraining cross-entropy loss or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The study reports geographical-probe results, not held-out pretraining loss, loss-law fits, compute-optimal parameter/token allocations, or extrapolations from small runs. Values cited from prior work are not recorded as results. The study also reports several qualitative trends from plots; these are noted as figure-only where applicable.
record.test_reason: The study measures how linear-probe recovery of geographic coordinates (test R2) changes with model size across many LM families. That is a downstream-style evaluation in a new setting, bearing on V6. It does not measure pretraining loss, fit a scaling equation, or test prediction from loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that geographic information is linearly recoverable even in tiny models and that probe performance consistently improves with size. They add that larger models are more heterogeneous (Gini), so scale amplifies geographic bias. Error correlates with latitude and country-name frequency but not with population.
record.recipe_differences: The study probes frozen representations with a Ridge regressor and evaluates geographic-coordinate prediction; it does not fit language-model loss scaling laws or examine compute-optimal training allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe performance varies across model families: BERT-Large is reported as comparable to Pythia-1B, XLM-R underperforms counterparts, and mGPT slightly underperforms equivalent-size Pythia models. The most performant layer is generally the last layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Gini heterogeneity of probe error across countries and continents increases with model size, and continent gaps do not shrink.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling amplifies geographic disparities in representation quality.

fits_no_version.finding: Probe error correlates negatively with latitude and with country-name frequency in the Pile, but not with population.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geographic representation quality tracks training-data frequency, not population.

fits_no_version.finding: Duplicating representation dimensions slightly lowers probe performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scale gains in probing are not due to dimensionality alone.

record.problems: The study measures a geographical probing task rather than held-out language-model loss or conventional downstream-task performance. Several cross-model trends and bias metrics are reported graphically without exact values in the text, and the paper does not fit or validate predictive scaling equations.
record.rows_left_out: No additional model-by-model Figure 2 or continent-by-size Figure 3 series values are recorded because the text does not state their individual values and the plots do not provide extractable values in the supplied text. The qualitative summaries are captured in r5 and r6.

untested.parts: No functional (power-law or other) fit of probe performance against scale, no extrapolation, and no prediction from pretraining loss. Only geographic probing is tested, not standard benchmarks.

missing.what: Per-suite R2-versus-size series for decoder and encoder suites, including the Llama-2 7B–70B points. These are declared in rows_left_out as plot-only.

record.verdict_notes: Whether linear-probe R2 counts as 'downstream task performance' is debatable. It is treated here as a weak, new-setting test of V6. The paper's 'scaling laws' title is loose: no law is fitted.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict losses of substantially larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation, and how either grows with compute.
Architecture effects on held-out language-model loss at a fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior of pretraining loss in other modalities or training regimes.
The study tests scale-related performance only on its geographical linear-probing task; it does not test conventional downstream task suites or prediction from pretraining loss.
Dependence of loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations on fitting choices, training schedules, or data.

rows.subject: Various decoder and encoder model suites
rows.operation_detail: Compare test-set geographical-probe R2 across model sizes and families.

conditions.value: GPT-2, OPT, Pythia, GPT-Neo, mGPT, Llama-2, BERT, RoBERTa, ELECTRA, DeBERTa-v3, and XLM-R

rows.value: The authors report that performance evolves consistently with model size regardless of architecture; exact series values are shown in Figure 2.
rows.note: This records the authors' qualitative summary across suites; the text does not provide individual Figure 2 values.

rows.subject: Pythia suite
rows.operation_detail: Measure geographical-probe mean-squared error by continent across model sizes.
rows.value: Performance increases consistently for every continent as model size increases; numerical values are shown in Figure 3.
rows.note: The prose states the trend for every continent but gives no exact values.

rows.subject: BERT-Large

conditions.value: Pythia-1B, described as three times larger

rows.value: BERT-Large is reported as equally accurate.
rows.note: The text reports a qualitative comparison, not an exact score.
rows.check: A cross-family comparison at different sizes, not a within-scale trend. It shows size alone does not fix performance, but 'partial' is not a meaningful state here.

rows.subject: XLM-R
rows.note: The paper gives no exact scores for this comparison.
rows.check: A cross-family offset (XLM-R below counterparts), not a measurement of the scale effect. The XLM-R size is not stated.

rows.subject: mGPT suite
rows.operation_detail: Compare geographical-probe performance with Pythia models at equivalent sizes.

conditions.value: Pythia models at equivalent model sizes

rows.note: The paper gives no exact scores for this comparison.
rows.check: A cross-family offset at equal size (mGPT slightly below Pythia), not a scale trend.

rows.subject: All tested models
rows.operation_detail: Concatenate each representation with itself to increase dimensionality without adding information.
rows.value: Performance is slightly worse for all tested models.
rows.note: The authors use this control to argue that the scale trend is not explained solely by representation dimensionality.
rows.check: The control result is as the authors intended: duplicating dimensions gave slightly worse performance. 'Absent' mislabels a control that worked; it bears on no version.

rows.subject: Pythia suite
rows.operation_detail: Calculate Gini coefficients for probe-error heterogeneity across countries and continents.
rows.value: Heterogeneity increases as model size increases; exact values are shown in Figure 4.
rows.note: The authors state that larger models have more heterogeneous probe performance.

rows.subject: Pythia suite
rows.operation_detail: Correlate location-level coordinate-prediction MSE with latitude.
rows.value: Error is negatively correlated with latitude, and this correlation decays slowly as model size increases.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 6 marks tests with p-values above 0.05; exact correlation values are not stated in the text.
rows.note: The text describes the direction and scale trend, but not exact coefficients.

rows.subject: Pythia suite
rows.operation_detail: Correlate location-level coordinate-prediction MSE with training-corpus country-name occurrences.
rows.value: Country-name occurrences are negatively correlated with error; the correlation is mild and below the significance threshold for the smallest model.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 6 marks tests with p-values above 0.05; exact coefficients are not stated in the text.
rows.note: The study reports the direction, describes the correlation as mild, and notes the smallest-model significance exception.

rows.subject: Pythia suite
rows.operation_detail: Correlate location-level coordinate-prediction MSE with population count.
rows.value: Population count is not correlated with error.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 6 marks tests with p-values above 0.05; exact coefficients are not stated in the text.
rows.note: The authors state that population count is not correlated with the error level.

relationships.condition: Geographic linear probing, within model suites (Pythia 14M–2.8B; GPT-2, OPT, GPT-Neo, mGPT, Llama-2, BERT-family encoders)
relationships.reason: Probe R2 rises monotonically with size in Pythia (r1-r4); authors report consistent improvement across suites (r5) and for every continent (r6).
relationships.display_finding: Probe R² increased monotonically with Pythia size, with consistent improvements reported across model suites and every continent.

relationships.condition: Across model families at a given size
relationships.reason: Parameter count does not predict performance across families: BERT-Large (336M) matches Pythia-1B, while XLM-R and mGPT underperform at similar sizes (r7-r9).
relationships.display_finding: BERT-Large at 336M matched Pythia-1B, while XLM-R and mGPT underperformed at similar sizes.
